title: Rooted forests, Hopf antipodes and subtraction recursion

items.title: Admissible-cut Hopf algebra for subdivergence forests
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal T$ be the set of isomorphism classes of finite nonempty rooted trees. A rooted tree is a finite connected acyclic graph with one distinguished vertex, the root; each edge is oriented from the vertex nearer the root (the parent) to the vertex farther from the root (the child). A forest is a finite multiset of rooted trees, including the empty forest $1$. Let $H=\mathbb Q[\mathcal T]$ be the commutative polynomial algebra generated by $\mathcal T$; its monomial basis consists of forests, and the degree of a forest is its total number of vertices.

For a rooted tree $t$, an admissible cut is a subset $C$ of its edges meeting every root-to-leaf path in at most one edge. Removing the edges of $C$ leaves one component containing the root; denote it by $R_C(t)$. The components on the child side of the cut edges form a forest denoted by $P_C(t)$. For the empty edge cut, set $P_{\varnothing}(t)=1$ and $R_{\varnothing}(t)=t$. Define the coproduct on a tree generator by
$$\Delta(t)=t\otimes1+\sum_{C\text{ admissible}}P_C(t)\otimes R_C(t),$$
where the sum includes the empty edge cut and retains multiplicities of distinct edge subsets. The term $t\otimes1$ is the separate virtual full cut above the root. Extend $\Delta$ multiplicatively to forests. Define $\varepsilon(1)=1$ and $\varepsilon(F)=0$ for every nonempty forest $F$. This specifies the rooted-tree subtraction model; it does not assert a canonical rooted-tree Hopf algebra or a graph-to-forest map for every Feynman graph.

references.title: Alain Connes and Dirk Kreimer, Hopf Algebras, Renormalization and Noncommutative Geometry, Communications in Mathematical Physics 199 (1998), 203–242
references.locator: Section 2.2, equations (65)–(71), printed pp. 30–31: finite rooted trees, admissible cuts, trunk, pruned forest, and the multiplicative coproduct.

references.title: Dominique Manchon, Hopf algebras, from basics to applications to renormalization, full lecture notes, arXiv:math/0408405v2
references.locator: Section II.9.3, printed pp. 42–44: admissible cuts, crown/trunk, and coassociativity by compatible two-level cuts; the present item fixes the Connes–Kreimer root orientation and commutative forest product.

items.title: Laurent-series target and pole projection for subtraction
items.statement: Let $K$ be a commutative unital $\mathbb Q$-algebra and let $\epsilon$ be a formal indeterminate. The Laurent-series algebra $A=K((\epsilon))$ consists of series $\sum_{n\ge N}a_n\epsilon^n$ for some integer $N$, with coefficients in $K$. Put $A_-=\epsilon^{-1}K[\epsilon^{-1}]$ (finite sums of strictly negative powers) and $A_+=\{\sum_{n\ge0}a_n\epsilon^n:a_n\in K\}$ (formal series of nonnegative powers). Then $A=A_-\oplus A_+$ as a $K$-module, and both summands are subalgebras, with $1\in A_+$. Define $R:A\to A_-$ by retaining exactly the strictly negative powers; $1-R$ is the projection onto $A_+$. The parameter $\epsilon$ is formal and carries no physical or empirical interpretation in this definition.

references.title: Dominique Manchon, Hopf algebras, from basics to applications to renormalization, full lecture notes, arXiv:math/0408405v2
references.locator: Section II.5, printed p. 35: the Laurent-series target, its splitting into negative and nonnegative powers, and projection onto the negative part.

items.title: Laurent pole projection satisfies the weight-minus-one identity
items.statement:
Let $K$ be a commutative unital $\mathbb Q$-algebra, let $\epsilon$ be formal, and put $A=K((\epsilon))$ with projection $R$ onto strictly negative powers. For all $x,y\in A$, $R$ satisfies
$$R(x)R(y)=R\bigl(R(x)y+xR(y)-xy\bigr).$$

references.title: Dominique Manchon, Hopf algebras, from basics to applications to renormalization, full lecture notes, arXiv:math/0408405v2
references.locator: Section II.5, Theorem II.5.1 proof, printed pp. 36–37: projection identity for a Laurent splitting, proved by decomposing each input into negative and nonnegative parts.

items.title: Admissible cuts give a connected graded Hopf algebra and recursive antipode
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal T$ be the isomorphism classes of finite nonempty rooted trees and $H=\mathbb Q[\mathcal T]$ their commutative polynomial algebra, graded by total vertices. An admissible cut is an edge subset meeting each root-to-leaf path at most once; $P_C(t)$ is its child-side forest and $R_C(t)$ its root-side tree. Use the coproduct $\Delta(t)=t\otimes1+\sum_C P_C(t)\otimes R_C(t)$, with the sum over admissible cuts including the empty cut, and counit $\varepsilon(1)=1$, $\varepsilon(F)=0$ for nonempty forests. The algebra $H$ is a connected graded bialgebra. Let $u$ be the algebra unit map and $m$ forest multiplication; use convolution $f*g=m(f\otimes g)\Delta$ on endomorphisms of $H$, with unit $u\varepsilon$. It has a unique two-sided convolution inverse $S$ of its identity map. For every rooted tree $t$ of positive degree,
$$S(1)=1,\qquad S(t)=-t-\sum_{\substack{C\ne\varnothing\\ C\text{ admissible}}}S(P_C(t))R_C(t).$$
The recursion is finite because each factor in every nonempty-cut term has fewer vertices than $t$. The antipode is multiplicative on forests. This is a theorem about the specified rooted-tree model and does not identify arbitrary Feynman graphs with rooted trees.

references.title: Alain Connes and Dirk Kreimer, Hopf Algebras, Renormalization and Noncommutative Geometry, Communications in Mathematical Physics 199 (1998), 203–242
references.locator: Section 2.2, equations (65)–(82), Lemma 1, printed pp. 30–33: rooted-tree coproduct, coassociativity proof, and antipode recursion.

references.title: Dominique Manchon, Hopf algebras, from basics to applications to renormalization, full lecture notes, arXiv:math/0408405v2
references.locator: Section II.3, Corollary II.3.2, printed p. 32, for the finite convolution-series antipode of a connected filtered bialgebra; Section II.9.3, printed pp. 42–44, for the compatible two-level-cut coassociativity argument.

items.title: Laurent subtraction factors a character into counterterm and finite characters
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal T$ be the isomorphism classes of finite nonempty rooted trees and $H=\mathbb Q[\mathcal T]$ their connected graded commutative Hopf algebra, graded by total vertices. Its coproduct is $\Delta(t)=t\otimes1+\sum_C P_C(t)\otimes R_C(t)$, where $C$ ranges over edge subsets meeting each root-to-leaf path at most once (including the empty cut), $P_C(t)$ is the child-side forest, and $R_C(t)$ is the root-side component; let $S$ be its antipode. Put $H_+=\bigoplus_{n>0}H_n$. Let $K$ be a commutative unital $\mathbb Q$-algebra, let $\epsilon$ be formal, and let $A=K((\epsilon))=A_-\oplus A_+$ split into strictly negative and nonnegative powers, with $R$ the projection onto $A_-$. A character is a unital algebra homomorphism $\phi:H\to A$. For each positive-degree homogeneous $h$, write $\widetilde\Delta(h)=\Delta(h)-h\otimes1-1\otimes h$ and define recursively
$$B_\phi(h)=\phi(h)+\sum_{\widetilde\Delta(h)}\phi_-(h_{(1)})\phi(h_{(2)}),\qquad \phi_-(1)=1,\qquad \phi_-(h)=-R B_\phi(h).$$
The sum is over the finite reduced coproduct and the recursion is degreewise finite. Define convolution by $f*g=m_A(f\otimes g)\Delta$, where $m_A$ and $u_A$ are the multiplication and unit maps of $A$, and put $\phi_+=\phi_-*\phi$. Then $\phi_-$ and $\phi_+$ are characters, $\phi_-(H_+)\subseteq A_-$ and $\phi_+(H)\subseteq A_+$, and the convolution inverse $\phi_-^{-1}=\phi_-\circ S$ exists with
$$\phi=\phi_-^{-1}*\phi_+.$$
This is an algebraic factorization for characters; it does not assert a graph-to-rooted-tree identification for actual Feynman graphs.

references.title: Dominique Manchon, Hopf algebras, from basics to applications to renormalization, full lecture notes, arXiv:math/0408405v2
references.locator: Section II.5, Theorem II.5.1 and its proof, printed pp. 35–37: degree-recursive Birkhoff decomposition, projection recursion, and character preservation under the Laurent splitting.
